correctness.rationale: The mixed-difference matrix has independent rows by an explicit discrete double-integration right inverse. Every active subset occurs with positive multipliers, so the Euclidean projection is locally an affine orthogonal projector with explicitly inverted active Gram matrix. Continuity and finite polyhedral stratification give the exact global Lipschitz maximum over active-face absolute row sums. The pure-Python Fraction certificate exhausts all 2, 16, and 512 subsets in sizes 2, 3, 4, checking symmetry, idempotence, active annihilation, per-cardinality maxima and uniqueness. An explicit rational finite input pair has ratio 9/4 with KKT multipliers >=397/400 and inactive slacks >=99/100. Embedding its five active constraints proves the stated n>=4 lower bound; no higher exact value is asserted.

value.rationale: For a natural supermodular/anti-Monge Frobenius least-squares operator, the complete additive pooling face is indeed worst at square sizes two and three but fails at the first square size four. The unique checkerboard instability is a motivated minimal structural counterexample and exact deterministic perturbation invariant, attained by displayed finite data, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The phenomenon persists as a lower bound on larger squares, identifying the first genuinely bivariate active-face mechanism relevant to shape-constrained matrix denoising.
